\subsection*{Circuit Complexity --- Meyer Complete: Results}

\begin{definition}[Signed edge encoding]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.edgeOf}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.edgeOf}
\leanok
For a Boolean value $s$ and a natural number $a$, the signed edge encoding is $-a-1$
when $s$ is true, and $a$ when $s$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sign of the Integer Encoding]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.sE_edgeOf}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.sE_edgeOf}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.edgeOf, Complexity.Meyer.sE}
\difficulty{4}
For $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and $a\in\mathbb{N}$, encode the pair by the
integer $-a-1$ when $s$ is true and by $a$ when $s$ is false. The sign indicator that is
true exactly for negative integers, applied to this encoding, equals $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding of a signed boundary position]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.aE_edgeOf}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.aE_edgeOf}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.aE, Complexity.Meyer.edgeOf}
\difficulty{4}
Let $s$ be a Boolean value and let $a$ be a natural number. Define $e=-a-1$ when $s$ is
true and $e=a$ when $s$ is false. Under the encoding $a(e)=-e-1$ for negative $e$ and
$a(e)=e$ otherwise, one has $a(e)=a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work-tape interpretation of symbolic answers]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.sv_true_some}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.sv_true_some}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.RW, Complexity.Meyer.decode_symBit, Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.sv, Complexity.Meyer.tabAns_sym_some, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, input $x$, and width $W$,
and let $\mathrm{Ans}$ assign Boolean values to table queries. Assume that for every
selector and $t,a<2^W$, these values agree with the corresponding selector answers on
the machine configuration reached after $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$.
For each work tape $h$, Boolean sign $s$, and $t,a<2^W$, the symbolic answer selecting
tape $h$ equals the symbol stored at displacement $(-1)^s a$ from that tape's head in
the configuration after $t$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Input-symbol interpretation of symbolic answers]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.sv_true_none}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.sv_true_none}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.RI, Complexity.Meyer.decode_symBit, Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.sv, Complexity.Meyer.tabAns_sym_none, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, input $x$, and width $W$,
and let $\mathrm{Ans}$ assign a Boolean value to each table selector and pair of
natural-number coordinates. Assume that whenever $t,a<2^W$, $\mathrm{Ans}$ agrees with
the corresponding selector answer on the machine configuration reached after $t$ steps
from its initial configuration on $x$, at coordinate $a$. Then for every sign $s$ and
every $t,a<2^W$, the symbolic answer for the absent-tape selector equals the input
symbol of that configuration at the position offset by $(-1)^s a$ from the input head,
with an out-of-range or boundary position interpreted as blank.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[State Answer Characterizes the Run]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.st_true}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.st_true}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.SS, Complexity.Meyer.tabAns_st, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.OutReg, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.OutReg.ofList, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean string,
and let $\mathrm{Ans}$ be a Boolean-valued function on selectors and two natural-number
indices. Suppose that for every selector $s$ and natural numbers $t,a$ with $t<2^W$ and
$a<2^W$, $\mathrm{Ans}(s,t,a)$ equals the tabulated answer for $s$ on the configuration
reached by $M$ on $x$ after $t$ steps, at index $a$. Then for every
state-and-output-register pair $\sigma$ and every $t<2^W$,
$\mathrm{Ans}(\mathrm{st}(\sigma),t,0)$ is true exactly when $\sigma$ is the state and
output-register summary of that configuration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[True claims determine the configuration]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.claims_true}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.claims_true}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.Rd, Complexity.Meyer.SS, Complexity.Meyer.avOf, Complexity.Meyer.claims, Complexity.Meyer.reads, Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.stA_NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.st_true, Complexity.Meyer.sv_true_none, Complexity.Meyer.sv_true_some, Complexity.Meyer.symvA_NumVal, Complexity.Meyer.tvOf, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.OutReg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a finite
Boolean input, and let $A$ be a Boolean answer table for state and tape-symbol queries
indexed by two natural numbers. Fix a width $W$ and assume that whenever $t,a<2^W$, the
table's answer at indices $(t,a)$ equals the machine's tabulated answer at time $t$ and
index $a$. For any $t<2^W$, natural numbers $a,j$, Boolean $b$, state-and-output pair
$\sigma$, and tuple $\rho$ of currently read symbols, if the numerical valuation
determined by $A,W,|x|,t,a,j,b$ makes the state-and-read claims for $\sigma,\rho$ true,
then $\sigma$ is the machine's actual state-and-output summary at time $t$, and $\rho$
is its tuple of read symbols at that time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Work Tape Consistency Check]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.workOK_true}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.workOK_true}

\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean
input, and let $W$ be a natural number. Suppose an answer table agrees with the
machine's actual tabulated answers for every selector and every time and address less
than $2^W$. If $t+1<2^W$, $h$ is a work-tape index, and $e$ is an integer whose encoded
address $a_E(e)$ satisfies $a_E(e)+1<2^W$, then the work-tape consistency check formed
from this table, at time $t$, tape $h$, and sign determined by whether $e<0$, evaluates
to true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Signed indexing of a Boolean list]
\lean{Complexity.Meyer.xin_sj}
\label{Complexity.Meyer.xin_sj}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.sgnZ, Complexity.Meyer.xhat}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean string and let $b : \mathbb{N} \to
\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ agree with $x$, so that $b(j)=x_j$ whenever $j<|x|$.
For every $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and $j\in\mathbb{N}$, the following
holds: if $s$ is true and $j>0$, both sides are undefined; otherwise, the expression
that returns $b(j)$ when $s$ is false and $j<|x|$, or when $s$ is true and $j=0<|x|$,
and is undefined in all other cases, equals the partial lookup of $x$ at the integer
position $1-j$ when $s$ is true and $1+j$ when $s$ is false.
\end{theorem}
